log.msg: Classified all 131 census rows for paging.css: 100 raw, 21 zero, 10 pre-existing token. Rule set: container gap/margin/padding between sibling blocks or list rows -> nearest rung (--gap-70/-50/-35/-25) or --gap by magnitude; a single control's own padding or icon-to-label gap stays em (matches the census's own 'under a quarter of gap = control territory' rule); the WHOLE toolbar family (both the older mode-toolbar and the real app toolbar, its rows/groups/picks/address/act/more) stays em too, extending the file's own written argument for the outer toolbar padding ('a toolbar is a control') to its children; two already-custom clamp() paddings (the hub's own content margin, the full-screen takeover padding) are deliberately shaped differently from --pad and were left with a note rather than forced onto the token.

CENSUS STALENESS: ai/2026-09-17/spacing-census/census.json's line numbers are wrong for paging.css past line ~1065 - an uncommitted edit (grid-auto-flow: dense, .paging-superseded, an @container paging-wall query, +37 net lines) landed in the working tree AFTER the census ran (paging.css mtime 23:44 on 9-17, the census's own task ran 22:05-22:41). Corrected 9 rows against the live file by grep before patching; decisions.mjs still keys by the census's own line numbers so the before/after table matches the census row set. Also found one live raw declaration the census never saw (.paging-superseded's padding-inline-start: 0.75em, added by that same uncommitted edit) - classified and noted the same as .paging-swapper-cap's letterform inset, outside the formal 131-row table.

FIRST PROOF ATTEMPT FAILED: full-page stylesheet-swap pixel diff came back 5-13% on every page, way over the 3% budget. Traced it with a red-overlay diff map (paging-diff-visual.mjs) rather than guessing: for the hub and make/ pages, 100% of the diff was confined to the left nav rail, with zero difference in the actual page content. Cause: .paging-app-rail/.paging-sec/.paging-grid's own gaps were measured to a fold budget (the file's own comment: 'the gaps came in, and the tiles are two-up sooner') and are repeated ~40 times down a long list - a rung's cqi growth compounds a fraction of a pixel per row into a multi-pixel sag by the bottom, which a dense small-text list renders as near-total text-edge mismatch. Reverted those three declarations back to their own em (control: rail chrome, fold-constrained) and the rail diff dropped to exactly zero.

SECOND FINDING, a real bug not just a measurement artifact: .paging-stage gets reused at a scaled-down font-size for live-miniature previews (.paging-shot-frame > .paging-stage { font-size: 0.6em }) - confirmed by DOM inspection, a .paging-canvas inside one of these miniatures computes to 9.024px font-size on a 1280 page. The OLD raw em values (gap: 0.7em etc.) scaled down WITH that local font-size; the new rungs (var(--gap-70) etc.) do not, because a custom property resolves from the framework's own clamp/cqi math, not the element's local font-size. So converting the stage's own content-wrapper classes (.paging-canvas, .paging-slot, .paging-pane, .paging-rows, and the content values a stage can hold: .paging-nest, .paging-expand, .paging-content-url) made every live-miniature preview on the hub disproportionately padded. Reverted these to their own em, same reasoning as a control: this content has to track a local, possibly-shrunk scale, not the site's fixed token grid. Re-testing now.

FINAL, after the three revert rounds above: of the 100 raw rows, 20 became a token/rung (19 rungs + 1 plain var(--gap)) and 75 stayed control-em with a note; the other 5 are 2 keywords (auto), one 1px hairline overlap, and two deliberately-shaped clamp()s left with a note. Combined with the 10 pre-existing tokens and 21 zero rows, paging.css is now 30 token/rung, 75 control-em, 21 zero, 5 raw (131 total, matches the census row count exactly). A file-wide regex re-scan for any padding/gap/margin declaration that is neither a var(), a zero/auto value, nor carrying a control/custom/hairline note found zero unclassified rows.

PROOF: PORT=8134, killed by its real Windows PID (24468, read from netstat, never by name) at landing. Four pages x two widths x stylesheet-swap (page.route() serves the reconstructed before-CSS then the real after-CSS on the same page, matching how ai.css proved itself the night before): hub, templates/blog/, mechanisms/swap/, make/, each at 1280 and 3440. FINAL RESULT: 0.000 percent of pixels differ on all eight shots, zero console errors on all eight loads.

Docs: one dated section in public/imagine/paging/doc/decisions.md (2026-09-18, the spacing ladder) with the before/after count and the three things the pixel-diff proof found and fixed. One line in the spacing census's own census.md (ai/2026-09-17/spacing-census/), striking through paging.css's old 100-raw count in the 'ten worst files' table with the new count and a link here. Fence held: only paging.css, doc/decisions.md and census.md's one line were touched - confirmed against git status, which shows a long list of OTHER paging/ files already modified by other concurrent minions (make/ especially) that this task never opened.

assign.outcome:
**paging.css's raw-number problem is mostly not a raw-number problem.** Of its 100 hand-typed spacing numbers (131 total spacing declarations, 1.7x the site's next-worst file), 20 became a token or a rung (`--gap-70` `--gap-50` `--gap-35` `--gap-25` `--gap`) and 75 stayed their own `em`, each with a one-line reason. The file is now 30 token/rung, 75 control-em, 21 zero, 5 raw (two keywords, a 1px hairline overlap, two deliberately-shaped `clamp()`s left alone on purpose).

**Most conversions failed the pixel-diff proof on the first pass, and that is the real finding.** The first cut converted 40 declarations; testing it with the same stylesheet-swap method `ai.css` used the night before found three genuine problems, not measurement noise: (1) the nav rail's own gaps were already tuned to a fold budget and a rung's growth compounds down ~40 repeated rows into a visible sag; (2) `.paging-stage` gets reused at a scaled-down font-size for live-miniature previews, and a rung does not reliably follow that local scale the way `em` does; (3) a handful of gaps simply grow too much at 3440 once they repeat several times on one page (the card wall, the toolbar-to-stage gap, the swap mechanism's own demo). All three were reverted to their own `em` rather than patched around.

**Proof, on a private server, four pages at two widths each:** the hub, `templates/blog/`, `mechanisms/swap/`, `make/` — **0.000% of pixels differ on all eight shots**, zero console errors.

- [`public/imagine/paging/paging.css`](/imagine/paging/) — the file, halved to 5 raw numbers
- [`doc/decisions.md`](/imagine/paging/doc/decisions.md) — the dated record: the rule, the three things the proof found, the fix
- [spacing census addendum](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/spacing-census/) — paging.css's line in the 'ten worst files' table, struck through

**Left, on purpose.** The other 1,064 bespoke numbers site-wide (generator.css 47, blogx.css 34, blog.css 32…) are untouched — this task was paging.css only. `ext/AITask/doc/file/ai.css.md` still describes ai.css's old multipliers, outside this fence. Two `clamp()` paddings (the hub's own content margin, the full-screen takeover padding) were left as their own deliberately-shaped clamps rather than forced onto `--pad`, which would have visibly changed their size.
